summary: Umpqua NF summit lookout: D-6 cupola cabin built 1923 after a 1921 telephone line; staffed through 1928; removed or destroyed 1952; no source describes remains.

facts.status_note: Cabin removed or destroyed in 1952 (sources disagree on which); no source found describes what remains on the summit

staffing.status: lookout staffed in 1928 (Paul Geddes named as forest service lookout)

access.note: Forest Service hiking trail still listed to the summit, Umpqua National Forest

visit.trail_note: Hiking trail to the summit; the last half mile is steep and rocky

events.note: Newspaper said R.C. Agee would take charge of the lookout station at Old Bailey; the Oregon lookouts history dates the lookout to 1917
Telephone line to the summit completed; insulated wire laid on the ground and taken up each fall
Temporary station planned (July 1921 report; opening not confirmed) with Arthur McIntosh of Riddle in charge
Newspaper credits the station with detecting a number of fires before they could do damage; no specific fires named
D-6 cupola cabin; parts cut in Roseburg, shipped to Medford, trucked to Diamond Lake and mule-packed to the summit
Paul Geddes named as the forest service lookout when 17 visitors reached the summit in July
Firetower.org says removed; firelookout.com and the Oregon lookouts history say destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org says the cabin was removed in 1952; firelookout.com and the Oregon Websites and Watersheds Project say it was destroyed that year. Both agree on 1952, so the story reports the disagreement over how it ended.

The Oregon Websites and Watersheds Project dates the lookout to 1917, the year a newspaper first names a station at the summit; firetower.org and firelookout.com date the cabin to 1923, which the story follows.

notes_for_editor: Brief access 'unknown' changed to public because a Forest Service trail to the summit is listed; the trail page does not describe the lookout site. No source read describes what remains on the summit today, so the story says so. The 1917 'established' date (ORWW) is treated as the first staffing, not the cabin date. Newspaper quotes are as reproduced on the Oregon lookouts site, not the original papers. No corrections proposed; the brief's status 'gone' and D-6 design fit the sources. Checked 2026-10-09: the 1921 temporary station was only planned (the July 1921 report says it 'will be provided'), so the story and event now say planned; the telephone line date rests on a January 28, 1922 report that says 'Last year'.
